Steep, Scary Stairs !
Feb 2026 • Couples
We had reservations and were eager to have dinner at Le Corto. We were out sightseeing and wanted to see just where it was and if we could safely walk there from the Park Hyatt. We found it, it was very close. We walked in to see the restaurant. 

A very nice young man took us up a very long steep flight of stairs to see the dining room. I was surprised as no one at the hotel who made our reservations or anyone on TripAdvisor made any mention of this. I asked the young man about the dining room downstairs and he said they do not serve dinner there. We are in seniors in good shape, but like to have a cocktail and or wine with our dinner. I was willing to give it a go, but it did give me pause and I wondered what someone with mobility issues would do. There is no elevator we were told. 

Turns out my husband became ill that afternoon so we had to cancel. They were very nice and accommodating with the cancellation but I still wonder about those scary stairs. There is no way a person with any kind of walking issues could navigate them.

A culinary pearl in the heart of Saigon.
Apr 2026 • Couples
Wonderful experience at this amazing location, everything about this restaurant is incredible,the service, the atmosphere and most importantly the food! The preparation and presentation of every dish was amazing, I always appreciate the details and in this restaurant they are definitely detail oriented. 
For starters we had the escargot which were perfect and oozing with rich butter and garlic, they were accompanied by slices of garlic bread. 
For our mains we went with the duck breast cooked to perfection and with the best New Zealand lamb chops I’ve had in a long while. Both dishes were accompanied by veggies and wonderful sauces. 
Finally, we were treated to their complimentary dessert which is just delicious. 
Our meal was accompanied by the sounds of a marvelous saxophonist with made our evening that much more unforgettable. 
This was our last dinner in HCMC and we certainly enjoyed what has been a great trip to this beautiful land.

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ A Culinary Highlight of Our Trip – Truly World-Class, We look forward to repeating.
Dec 2025 • Family
We visited Le Corto last week as a family—mom, dad, and son—traveling from abroad, and it was without question one of the most memorable dining experiences of our entire trip.

From the very first bite, we knew we were in for something special. The French Snail (Ốc Pháp), baked in fragrant parsley and garlic butter, was rich, comforting, and perfectly balanced. The Homemade Pâté en Croûte, served with young lettuce salad, onion marmalade, and condiments, was beautifully crafted—classic French technique done flawlessly. The salmon platter was fresh, elegant, and ideal for sharing.

For the main courses, every dish impressed us. The Long An Barbary Duck was outstanding—seven days dry-aged, expertly roasted duck breast, paired with young carrots and a vibrant orange sauce. The Beef Wellington was cooked to perfection, tender and flavorful, complemented by truffle mashed potatoes, asparagus, and a luxurious Périgourdine sauce. The Pan-Fried Seabass was equally impressive—delicate, fresh, and beautifully presented.

Dessert was a true spectacle and a joy for our son to watch. The Crêpes Suzette Flambé, cooked over high fire right in front of us, was both theatrical and delicious, while the Crème Brûlée had the perfect crackling top and silky smooth custard. We paired our meal with Château Le Grand Verdus Bordeaux Blanc, which elevated the entire experience.

What truly made (Our ALL YOU CAN EAT) exceptional was the service. The crew was attentive, warm, and professional, making us feel genuinely welcome. Special thanks to Lyn and Troung, whose hospitality, knowledge, and care turned a wonderful lunch into an unforgettable family memory.

Le Corto is not just a restaurant—it’s an experience. For travelers looking for refined French cuisine, impeccable service, and an atmosphere that feels both elegant and welcoming, this place is a must-visit. We sincerely hope to return on our next trip.

Family Friendly and Delicious
Apr 2025 • Family
I had lunch with my family of 5 here and it was incredible! My family and I have actually never had French food before, but we were feeling adventurous.

We had the mackerel as an appetizer and chose the a la carte duck breast for the entree, which was the best duck we had ever tasted. Chef Sakal explained to us how the ducks came from the Mekong Delta and how they were dry aged and roasted. The duck skin was crispy like Peking duck, but the meat was incredibly tender and juicy. It is a must-order dish. We also tried the escargot which was seasoned perfectly and very enjoyable with the garlic and sourdough bread. My boyfriend has a previous bad experience with escargot at another restaurant but the escargot at Le Corto completely changed his attitude towards the dish. Finally, we had crepes (which were lit on fire!) with coconut ice cream and a dessert box with delicious truffles and small pastries. I think it is so rare to find a restaurant that excels in both entrees and desserts, but this one did!

The ambiance of the restaurant was so cozy but also very elegant. As an American, I noticed that many French restaurants in the USA seem very pretentious and stuffy, so their cuisine is often inaccessible to many people. At Le Corto, the waitstaff and Chef Sakal treat their patrons like family while still providing a classy and high quality experience. This restaurant is truly a gem in Saigon and I would not hesitate to eat here with my family again. I would eat at any restaurant of Chef Sakal's in Vietnam!

The service was impeccable - highly professional and dignified. I'm sorry not to remember our servers' names, but we were there on February 3rd, so please refer.
They offer a large wine list and larger whiskey bar. Make your reservations for the "upper floor," not the ground floor, which seems to be more of a whiskey bar atmosphere. 
 Note that the restaurant is on a small dark alleyway, and difficult to locate. Suggest that you take a taxi and show the driver on your phone app exactly where the restaurant is, so that he can drop you right in front. It is just off a main boulevard, and depending where you are staying, very safe to walk back to your hotel, but I would not recommend trying to locate the restaurant on your own.

3. Desert: Baked Alaska for 2. Its taste was great, however, we wished to have more time to eat it all since it was too much for 2.

The Worst Meal in Memory
May 2022
I visited Le Corto Friday, 5/13 at 630PM. This was the worst meal I have ever had from a seemingly "upscale" restaurant. 
The dining room was pretty empty when I arrived--I guess it was early in the night still. Shortly after sitting down, I ordered a Negroni. I was not offered water. I waived a server down and asked for water and was asked if I wanted sparkling or still. I asked for sparkling. 10 minutes passed, still no water. I waived down another server, asked again, and they promptly brought a bottle, which they presented to me. The water they poured was entirely flat. I did not hear a seal break on the twist top when the bottle was opened.
When the primary server came by, I pointed this out and she grabbed a new bottle--an entirely different brand--which she opened by the table and poured (it was sparkling).
Meanwhile, a server came to take my food order; I picked the tasting menu. They were very confused and started to ask me to "pick" the cold or hot starter (the tasting should include both). The primary server ran over and stepped in.
The cold starter was inedible. It was some mound of crab and squid that smelled and tasted like it could have even been from a can. Potentially in an attempt to hide the taste, the mound of fish was mixed heavily with some mayo-like cream that left it wet and mushy.
The primary server came by and asked if I did not like the dish. I told her it did not taste at all fresh. She later returned saying "the chef apologized and acknowledged it was not fresh" for some reason I cannot remember. She offered to comp me a glass of wine.
I saw her open the bottle of wine (re-corked) and there was an audible "pop" from across the room. I then watched her take her mask down off her nose to smell the bottle, probably in an attempt to check freshness.
She brought the bottle to my table to pour at which point I noticed it was less than half full. Remember, this was the beginning of the dinner service and the restaurant was empty...it surely was open for a long time, and it definitely tasted like it.
The foie gras was fine. I ran out of water and again had to ask two different servers before someone brought me more water (waiting almost 10 minutes between requests).
The filet was so disappointing. Even the lousiest restaurants generally cook a filet reasonably well. I don't know what the issue was here--it was cooked rare+, as I had asked, but the meat was tough and tasteless.

This was the most disappointing meal I have had in memory. I don't know why I didn't walk out after the cold starter--the writing was on the wall. I'm not sure how this place has so many good reviews. Sad!

A Moveable Feast in Saigon
Dec 2019
I’ve dined at Le Corto on two occasions and the food and service has been consistently good on both visits. On a pure food perspective, Le Corto would most certainly merit one Michelin star if the guidebook ever came to Saigon. 

On my most recent visit, both my dining partner and I ordered the Caviar menu which was 1.5M VND, I believe. The amuse bouche was a dollop of caviar on top of a black potato made to appear as a truffle on a bed of popcorn. Rather an inauspicious start, I thought, but I needn’t have worried. The remainder of the courses were less “whimsical."

The meal in earnest started with the first course of Hokkaido scallop ceviche marinated with green chilis and topped with caviar Kaspia. A delicate intersection of scallop with just enough heat from the chilis.

The second course was oven baked snow fish, tofu “mousseline” and caviar caspiar. Was unsure what snow fish is but it has the same taste and texture of cod or sablefish. The mousseline was a bit too mushy for my taste but the fish was cooked perfectly (although it’s practically impossible to overcook code).

The main entree and star of the meal was a deliciously prepared Canadian lobster, mussels, seasonal vegetables topped again with caviar, and served with sauce à l’américaine (sumptuously prepared with lobster stock, tomatoes, and wine reduction). As good as anything I’ve ever eaten in San Francisco, New York, or Paris.

The dessert was some sort of sorbet which I do not remember the particulars although I did take a picture (posted here).

Overall, probably the best “western” meal I’ve had in Vietnam. The pacing of the food was perfect, and the Vietnamese wait staff friendly and knowledgable. My only critiques, was that the restaurant decor was a bit too informal for the level of the meal. I felt like I was eating at the Cheesecake Factory or PF Chang's. Also, I saw what appeared to be a European restaurant manager milling about talking to the staff but not once did I see him interact with any of the guests. My table included even though ours was a birthday dinner and had ordered the special tasting menu. Small things, I know, but things you would not see back in the US at a restaurant of this caliber.

If visiting Saigon, I do highly recommend visiting Le Corto. There may be more expensive restaurants in the city but you will not enjoy a better meal at any price.

A fallen angel - food still good but now absurdly expensive. Not worth it at all!
Oct 2019
Le Corto has until recently been an oasis of excellent, often very sophisticated French cuisine, priced not low but reasonable for ambitious dishes served in a pleasant, low-light atmosphere. Now someone has gotten very greedy - dishes are often VERY small, with the costlier elements minimised (f.x. try the veal and receive two (small) pillbox sized cuts)...and all at completely grotesque prices; 75 USD for a so-called 'tasting menu', which is just a selection of 2 starters, a main course and a dessert from the menu. Should you wish to accompany your dinner with a glass of red wine the wine-by-the glass selection is 4 low-shelf supermarket wines of which one was even out of stock (In comparison, a 5 course menu at the recently nominated 'Worlds Best Restaurant, the RTB Hutong in Beijing is 97 USD - incl. serving in an ancient temple and a 950 item wine list). And then there is the lighting - Le Corto has black walls with mirrors, all intended to create an intimate atmosphere with dimmed lighting. Now, they have, perhaps in pursuit of further profit increases, installed very bright hair-white spots that glare in in the eyes, depending on where your are sitting around table. So, with the exception of the very capable service staff, this place has, sadly, gone totally off the rails - unless you are happy to be a fool for your money. On an optimistic note, Le Corto apparently has a new restaurant manager - hopefully he will be able to bring the place back to its former glory.

The 3 mains we ordered to share, however, were good but not exactly on point. The veal sweetbreads and wagyu flank steak were good but not super outstanding (hence this rating), but duck confit was significantly salty (and we do have quite a tolerance for salt). The mash potatoes which we selected to go with the steak were significantly gluey, an indication of it being over-processed; upon checking, it did appear to have been put thru a machine, thereby explaining the texture. The same mash was used to make the fried potato morsels for the veal dish, which had the same effect, altho somewhat offset by the crisp exterior. The recommended dessert was the apple tart, which was really pretty - apple slices arranged like a flower petal on a crisp pastry base - taste again was good but not super outstanding.

They have some reasonably-priced wines (given this was fine dining) so its not too bad - although the wait staff are extremely (maybe a bit too much) attentive at refilling your glass!

Looking for a good French restaurant in Ho Chi Minh city we followed the concierge recommendation and we were not disappointed. While not large, the restaurant is comfortably spaced (not a bistro) and quite nicely appointed.
The menu was sufficiently broad to meet most culinary desires and, as with most French restaurants, the portions were appropriate for a single meal. The pan-fried scallops and black cod are definitely worthy of a try.
Also particularly impressive was the wine list which had ample selections of International wines and with the nanagers/sommeliers help we chose an excellent Barolo.
The dessert menu, while we did not try, looked sufficiently tempting to satisfy the most discriminating sweet tooth connoisseur.

Was in Ho Chih Minh city for business and decided to try some French restaurant.

I had a reservation and on entering the restaurant I was immediately “transferred” into a twilight zone of mixed bright red modern furnitures against a grey and brick layered wall. Stunning and with expectations of the unexpected.

I was early and was the only guest but my waiter a Mr Bruce was impeccable when it came to service. Like a dedicated butler he was near perfect. 

Wine list was not as exciting but bearable. I ordered a house carafe of Gerard Bertrand Cabernet Sauvignon. Modestly dry with a better bodied than expected.

The menu was extensive. It was filled with known French favorites and very intriguing new items. 

I decided to try the new items and ordered as follow:

Appetizers - I had the raw sea scallops, marinated red tuna and mashed avocado over wasabi sauce. It was soooooo beautifully refreshing. The scallop was skillfully flattened and sits on a tuna steak over mash avocado. Uniquely refreshing, with deep flavors and was an absolutely delight so full of identity and taste. Tangible but melts with each bite. This was a winner !!!

For my main, I chose the Veal sweetbread with morel mushrooms crushed potatoes and truffle sauce. This was another winner !! It was the dish that - one will expect the unexpected!!! 

The veal was deep fried with house flour and its crispness seats over a cake of crushed potatoes. The “killer” in this dish must have been the truffle sauce. So thick creamy and literally forms a remarkably tasteful cream melting the crispy sweetbread. Never have I eaten sweetbread in this manner. 

I could have gone on.. but decided that I should perhaps close on a high winning note... without any blemish - the dessert list was not particularly enticing... hahaha. 

I settled for a house made lemon sorbet to wash my palate and crowning the night, with some green tea to finish over the wonderful taste of my French meal in Saigon - an old but not forlorn but rather a very vibrantly spectacular French cuisine - I hope the best is yet to be. 

Very Well done !!!!

Absolute BEST BEST French restaurant in HCMC!! Excellent food, service, and decor! A gem in the city not to be missed!
Apr 2018
I eat here every time I'm in HCMC. Chef Sakal is an incredibly talented chef and the food speaks for itself-- every item on the menu is delicious, he gets the flavours right. I have eaten dinner at Le Corto a few times now and have thoroughly enjoyed every visit. You can really tell that they use high quality ingredients. The amuse bouches are always a delight. My favourite is the lamb, but the smoked pigeon cooked inside a cacao shell is also really nice. I like that there are a lot of vegetable options on the menu, I've had a delicious artichoke salad with a very nice mustard dressing that is fresh and flavourful.

I had my birthday dinner here with a girlfriend once and not a lot of people know this but you can special order a vanilla, chocolate, and raspberry ice cream cake! It was not only beautiful and creative (the chef lit if on fire, literally!) but it was also the most delicious ice cream cake I've ever had--not too sweet, just perfect!! 

Dinner is fantastic but the brunch is also very good, I highly recommend trying it at least once--great quality and very good value. Honestly, it's better than a lot of hotel brunches in the city and I've stayed at a lot of 5 star hotels in HCMC so I have a decent benchmark. Oysters, lobster, quality ham and delicious cheeses! 

Don't miss out on this restaurant! Food, service, and cozy beautifully thought out decor is worth the trip! I can't wait to be back! Thanks Le Corto for a great experience!!!!

Staff were exceptional being very observant without being overbearing. Polite and adept at watching the room so we never found ourselves trying to catch the eye of the staff for service. Our party was there from 7pm until way after closing time and retiring to the small outside balcony area. At no point did the staff make us feel we needed to leave so they could lock up as is often the case in some places. They asked us if we would not mind settling the bill but could stay if we liked. That is service and has guaranteed many return visits from me and I will recommend. I have read some reviews saying it is high priced for what it is. I disagree completely. We chose from the A’lacarte menu and had 2 bottles of good wine with the charge coming in at much less than you would pay in some other places in HCM and a lot under what you would pay for anything comparable in cities such as HK. 
If you have a group or a couple looking for a little privacy I recommend booking the sofa table upstairs. The 1+1 tables down the middle are a little close if you do not want other guests overhearing you,

Elaborative French feast
Dec 2022
Long heard of praises on Le Corto as the best French restaurant in Ho Chi Minh City and finally got a chance to try. Reservation was smooth by email and staff is careful to details. Service is impeccably top-notch. However, it is the food that delivers and our meal is simply perfect.

Oyster gratin is a lovely start of our French feast. The shellfish is fresh from Nha Trang and full of umami. The rich cream sauce adds color to the beautiful oyster. 

Truffle soup is a clear, flavorful consumme with beef, foie gras and vegetable. An appealing middle course before the entree. 

Tournedos Rossini, a cornerstone of French haute cuisine, is flawless. Chateaubriand remains tender and juicy with the oily aroma of foie gras and an appetizing jus. 

Chocolate souffle is a wonderful end to the meal. 

Price is still modest for tourists given the quality of presentation and delivery. Will definitely recommend.
